judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of "Project" piles up broad alternatives — "any work, service or activity which is separately planned, financed, or identified by the commission" — whose reach is genuinely contestable, and the trailing qualifiers ("can be established and utilized independently", "considered as a separate entity for purposes of evaluation") may modify only the second limb or both. Whether a private activity such as gas drilling is a "project" turns entirely on this wording, so ambiguity is real and namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition feeds directly into Section 3.8's approval requirement and Section 11.1/11.2's comprehensive-plan condition, and its breadth sits uneasily against Section 1.5's pledge to preserve existing state agency functions and Section 3.8's separate "substantial effect" threshold. That interplay creates a plausible whole-instrument tension over how far commission jurisdiction reaches.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "No project having a substantial effect on the water resources of the basin" uses two vague operators — "substantial effect" and later "substantially impair or conflict with the comprehensive plan" — with no defined boundary, and the mandatory "shall approve ... whenever it finds" sits against the discretionary "may modify" and "may disapprove." The scope of "any person, corporation or governmental authority" against the defined term "project" adds a further general-vs-specific question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its reach depends on the Section 1.2(g) definition of "project" and it must be read with Sections 11.1(b) and 11.2(b), which condition expenditure on prior inclusion in the comprehensive plan rather than on case-by-case approval; Section 1.5's preservation of existing agencies also pulls the other way. That is a specific and litigable relational tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals are aspirational narrative, listing purposes and population projections, and contain no operative obligation whose terms could be applied; the closing covenant is definite as to the mode of adoption. Their generality invites use as interpretive aid rather than as a source of independent ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Recitals of this breadth can be pressed against operative limits such as Section 1.5 (preserving existing agencies) or Section 3.8, so a recital-versus-text argument is conceivable, though nothing here squarely contradicts an operative provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short title provision with a stray double period; the duplicated punctuation is a typographic slip that changes nothing about meaning. Nothing here is capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses "This Act" whereas Section 1.2(c) defines "Compact" as Part I of the act, a mild terminological mismatch of no operative consequence. Otherwise consistent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definitional preamble includes the escape hatch "except as may be otherwise required by the context," which by design leaves room to displace any defined term. That is a familiar, and mildly litigable, flexibility clause but its function is understood.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs all of Section 1.2 and is consistent with the rest; no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Area of drainage into the Delaware River and its tributaries, including Delaware Bay" is a hydrologically determinate boundary; the only latent question is the precise edge of drainage area. The wording is otherwise definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.7's in-basin/out-of-basin jurisdictional division and with Article 10; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A purely nominal definition identifying the body created by the compact; no term admits of two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.1 which creates the commission; no tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Compact shall mean Part I of this act" is a definite, single-meaning definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Part II provisions that speak of "this Act" and "the Compact" separately, which is coherent; no conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Net induced adverse effects, whether or not compensated for" is a vague economic concept with no measurement standard, and "indirect expenditures" has no boundary. The term "cost" so defined could be applied very differently by different parties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds Sections 11.4 and 12.2 on cost allocation and Section 4.3's assessment ceiling of "actual benefit," but nothing there contradicts the definition. Consistent with the whole.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is a sprawling catch-all with enumerated specifics followed by "any other uses of any of them" and "necessary, useful or convenient," a classic ejusdem generis setting whose outer reach is uncertain. "Facility" could plausibly be argued narrower than its literal text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with Sections 3.6(a), 4.1 and 12.2 without contradiction, though its breadth mirrors the same jurisdictional expansiveness as "project." No specific conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any appropriate branch, department, bureau or division thereof, as the case may be" imports the vague qualifier "appropriate," but in context it is a housekeeping definition. Little practical scope for dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.2(h) and the Part II federal reservations; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite enumeration of the five parties; no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.6(a), which speaks of termination by "signatory states" only, a distinction that is deliberate rather than contradictory. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Water and related natural resources ... including related uses of land" is broad, and "related" has no stated limit, which could be argued over in a jurisdictional dispute. Still, its function as an inclusive definition is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Sections 3.8 and 6.2 (land use standards) and with Section 6.2(a)'s preservation of state zoning power; no direct contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare introductory phrase to legislative findings; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the whole; findings are recital-like and no operative provision contradicts the introduction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A declaratory finding of public purpose in general terms; no operative term requiring application.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.3(b) and the preamble; no tension identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Declares a "joint exercise of such powers of sovereignty," a general statement of purpose rather than an applied standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside Section 5.5 and Section 1.5, which preserve state authority; a party could argue the finding overstates the joint character, but no squarely inconsistent operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The statement that "a single administrative agency is therefore essential" is a policy finding, definite in expression though not operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It could be invoked as a recital against Section 1.5's preservation of existing agencies and Section 5.5's reservation of state power, a genuine if modest recital-versus-text pull.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A factual finding about adequacy of supply, with a run-on lacking punctuation before "and ever increasing economies," but its meaning remains discernible. No operative term at stake.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Article 10's protected-area and emergency-shortage machinery, which presupposes shortages; that is a recital-versus-operative tension of the kind courts note. Still fairly weak.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of purposes closing with "equal and uniform treatment to all water users who are similarly situated" — "similarly situated" is vague, but the clause is declaratory. Limited application risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Could be pressed against Section 4.3's benefit-based assessments or Section 3.3's allocation power, but nothing squarely contradicts it. Largely consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite reservation of congressional power expressed in standard "nothing herein shall be construed" form; the terms are broad but their operation is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly cross-referenced by Sections 11.1 and 15.1(b) and 15.1(t), which harmonize with it; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "To the fullest extent it finds feasible and advantageous" is a soft, discretion-laden standard, and "not inconsistent with the compact" leaves the boundary to be judged. The provision is more hortatory than mandatory despite "authorized and directed."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is invoked by Sections 7.4(b) and 8.2(b) as a constraint on commission operation, and can be argued against the broad jurisdiction implied by Section 3.8 and Section 1.3(c). Some relational tension, not a clear conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The renewal notice window is self-contradictory as written: "not later than 20 years nor sooner than 25 years prior to the termination" inverts the limits, a mechanical error that makes the timing requirement impossible to satisfy literally. That is a namable drafting defect on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It relates to Section 1.6(b) on dissolution and to Section 2.1's "succession for the duration of this compact," which are consistent; the defect is internal to the sentence rather than relational.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in operation, leaving the manner of winding up to an act of Congress; no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on the flawed paragraph (a) it cross-references, but is otherwise consistent with Section 2.1. No independent conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear creating provision; "body politic and corporate" is a settled term of art.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.1 and 15.1(m), which qualify the commission's status for federal-law purposes without contradicting its creation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The phrase "to serve during the term of office of the President" is definite on its face, though the annotation shows it was later amended. Nothing internally ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: As enacted it was directly inconsistent with Section 15.1(d) ("shall serve at the pleasure of the President") — the endnote itself acknowledges the inconsistency, which is exactly a Category 2 conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The appointment, term and vacancy mechanics are stated definitely, with "unless otherwise provided by law of the signatory party" as a clear carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with Section 2.5's one-vote rule and Section 15.1(d)/(r) on the federal alternate; New York § 631 supplies a substitute chain without contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for necessary expenses" is definite, with only the ordinary softness of "necessary."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(r) expressly overrides this for the federal member ("notwithstanding" Sections 2.4 and 2.6), a stated exception rather than a hidden conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "A majority of the membership" could be read as majority of the full five-member body or of those present, a small but real ambiguity given the second sentence says "at any meeting." The term is namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the unanimity requirements in Sections 3.3(a) and 13.3(b)(2) and the "full membership" language in Section 14.5(a), which suggests deliberate differentiation rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Internal organization and officer-election provisions are stated definitely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(r) modifies it for federal advisors by express "notwithstanding" language; New York § 632 designates the advisor consistently. No hidden conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Necessary or convenient to effectuate its powers" is elastic, and the final sentence's "such power" is ambiguous as to whether the consent requirement covers all extraterritorial action or only the sale of water. That is a genuine referential ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with Section 1.2(e), which contemplates facilities "within or without the basin," and with Article 9's marketing powers; the consent proviso could be argued to cut against those. Modest tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: General mandate language ("develop and effectuate plans, policies and projects") with no applied threshold; broad but not internally ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article 13 and Section 3.2; no conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A directory introduction cross-referencing Article 13; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 13.1–13.3, which it incorporates by reference.
judgments.clause_name: Section 3.2 Comprehensive Plan, Program and Budgets (introduction)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires consultation with "water users and interested public bodies"; "interested" is unbounded but the duty is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors Section 13.1's fuller consultation duty, which additionally names public utilities — a slight incompleteness rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but definite specification of the program's contents; "reasonably foreseeable period as the commission may determine" is self-defining discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nearly duplicates Section 13.2, which adds an "ensuing six years" default; the two are harmonizable but overlapping.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite budget-adoption requirement with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 13.3(a) and (b); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Grants allocation power "in accordance with the doctrine of equitable apportionment," importing an external and contestable legal standard, and "as need appears" is vague. The imported doctrine is a namable source of dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Section 3.3(b), which says no allocation shall be "deemed to constitute an apportionment" — a tension between the granted power and its disclaimer that a court could be asked to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The emergency proviso is carefully bounded (unanimous consent, limited time), though "drought or catastrophe" and "as may be necessary" carry ordinary vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coordinates with Sections 3.4 and 3.5 and with New York § 633's consent requirement; the scheme is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The disclaimer that allocations are neither prior appropriation nor apportionment, coupled with a proviso preserving covenant power, is complex but each element is stated definitely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It arguably pulls against the Section 3.3 introduction's grant of power to allocate "in accordance with the doctrine of equitable apportionment," a reconcilable but genuine internal pull.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any proper party deeming itself aggrieved" and "out-of-basin diversion" are the operative triggers; "proper party" is undefined and could be contested. The de novo Supreme Court route is otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.4's exception for proceedings by "a proper party" and with the general judicial review clauses; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A waiver with two stacked exceptions cross-referencing decree paragraphs; dense but the terms are specific and the referents identified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with Sections 3.3 and 3.5 and New York § 633; the exception for Section 3.3 proceedings is expressly reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Except as specifically provided in Sections 3.3 and 3.4 ... nothing in this compact shall be construed" is a definite savings formula, with "without limitation thereto" preceding a list — a mild general-versus-specific setup.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly harmonized with Sections 3.3 and 3.4 and cross-referenced by Section 3.8; consistent.
judgments.clause_name: Section 3.5 Supreme Court Decree; Specific Limitations on Commission (introduction)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Impede or interfere with" the decree rights is somewhat open-textured but tied to an identified decree.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Section 3.5 introduction and Section 14.14(a)'s exclusion of decree-related property from condemnation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat prohibition on fees for decree-permitted diversions; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforced rather than contradicted by Section 15.1(b), which similarly limits Section 3.7 charging power.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but specific catalogue of the jurisdiction withheld absent consent; no genuinely ambiguous operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.8's "subject to the provisions of Sections 3.3 and 3.5" carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, clear prohibition on serving as river master absent consent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.3(a)'s reference to consulting the river master; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-word permissive introduction; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the enumerated powers that follow and with Section 3.6(h)'s catch-all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long verb-string power qualified by "necessary, convenient or useful for the purposes of this compact," a standard the commission itself determines; broad but conventionally worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Must be read with Section 3.5(a)'s prohibition on projects interfering with the decree and with Sections 7.4(b)/8.2(b)'s no-operation-if-others-available limits; harmonizable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Including without limitation thereto" followed by a list of specifics is the classic general-versus-enumerated setup, leaving the standard-setting power's outer reach uncertain. The catch-all's reach is nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It intersects with Section 6.2(a)'s preservation of state and local zoning power and with Section 11.2; no squarely contradictory term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Research and data powers listed illustratively with "including without limitation thereto"; the breadth is unlikely to be contested because the power is benign.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6(d)-(f) and 14.12; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "When and as needed for water uses, flood warning, quality maintenance or other purposes" ends in an open catch-all, but the power is informational and permissive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.4 on flood warnings; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite grant of investigative power tied to formulating the comprehensive plan.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 13.1; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Publication and reporting power stated definitely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 14.12's reporting duty; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad borrowing/aid-acceptance authority conditioned on lawfulness; "as the commission may deem necessary or desirable" is self-referential discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 12.1, 14.1(a)(2) and 14.13; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure catch-all — "such other and different powers" plus "reasonably implied therefrom" — following an enumerated list, which is precisely the general-versus-specific tension that generates expressio unius arguments. Its reach cannot be bounded from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Sections 1.5, 3.5 and 15.1(a)'s limits on undertaking projects, an implied-powers argument could be said to swallow those constraints; a genuine if arguable relational point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Rate-setting authority "without regulation or control by any department, office or agency of any signatory party" is definite in operation, though "facilities which it may own or operate" is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(b) expressly narrows Section 3.7 for pre-existing free withdrawals and navigation, and Section 3.5(b) bars decree-related fees — express qualifications rather than conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The phrase "but with limitation thereto" is an evident mechanical error for "but without limitation thereto," and it reverses the sense of whether the following list is exhaustive. That is a namable defect affecting meaning.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Advise, consult, contract, financially assist, or otherwise cooperate" ends with a general catch-all but the power is plainly facilitative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 1.5 and 11.5; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Or for any other purpose" is a wholly open catch-all appended to specific activities, leaving its reach indeterminate. Still, the underlying power to employ agencies is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 1.5's directive to utilize existing agencies and Section 11.5; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "So far as consistent with the comprehensive plan" is a workable qualifier; the clause is otherwise definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 13.1's plan-adoption process; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear power to qualify as a sponsoring agency under federal legislation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.6(g) and 15.1(o); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive authority to constitute advisory committees with an illustrative membership list; no operative ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.6's advisor provision and New York § 632; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Without limitation thereto" precedes a facility list and "such off-river sites as it may find appropriate" is discretionary, but the grant of water-supply power is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.5's bar on "the business of distributing water" limits this article, an express carve-out that harmonizes rather than conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long purpose list ending in "and other purposes," a catch-all whose reach is unbounded; the core power is nevertheless clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 6.1 and 5.1 on storage/release and pollution dilution; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition on diminishing augmented flow is definite, with three specified exceptions rather than a catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with Article 10's withdrawal controls and Section 3.5's decree protections, which supply the "duly authorized" exceptions; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Specially benefited thereby to a measurable extent" and the cap at "actual benefit to any water user" are both vague valuation standards that two parties could apply very differently. The terms are namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Section 3.5(b)'s bar on charges for decree-permitted diversions and Section 11.3's reserved state taxing power; those are limits rather than contradictions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Review and consider all existing rights, plans and programs ... which are pertinent" imposes a procedural duty whose adequacy is judged by the vague word "pertinent." The public hearing requirement is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 13.1 and 14.4(b) on hearings; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso against engaging "in the business of distributing water" is a line whose location — transmission versus distribution — could genuinely be argued. That phrase is a namable boundary problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Section 9.3's bar on direct sale to consumers and limits Section 4.1; the scheme is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Control potential pollution and abate or dilute existing pollution" is broad but the grant is plainly permissive and clear in scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.2–5.5 and with Section 15.1(k)'s preservation of federal pollution functions; no conflict.

"Injuriously affect" is a namable ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Section 5.5's preservation of stricter state law and Section 15.1(k)'s federal reservation, which are compatible; no direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The covenant sets aspirational water-quality descriptors — "satisfactory condition," "after reasonable treatment," "free from unsightly or malodorous nuisances" — that are vague as enforceable standards. These terms are namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.2 and 5.5; the covenant supplements rather than contradicts commission authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enforcement machinery stated with specificity as to orders, timing and courts; only "reasonable time for construction" is soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.2, 14.17 and the judicial-review clauses; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear savings clause preserving stricter state pollution law; "additional conditions and restrictions" is a plain formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Section 5.2's grant of commission jurisdiction to "assume" pollution control and Section 10.8's supersession rule, raising a mild question about which prevails when state law is more stringent. Reconcilable but arguable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "As it may deem necessary or desirable" and "in such manner, at such times, and under such regulations as the commission may deem appropriate" are broad self-judging standards but the power is unmistakable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.2(a) and 6.2–6.4; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The label "recommended standards" against the power to "adopt, amend and repeal" them creates uncertainty about whether the standards bind anyone. That tension is namable within the sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.3 requires commission acquisitions to "be in accord with the standards adopted and promulgated pursuant to Section 6.2," and Section 6.2(b) contemplates enforcement aid, which pulls against "recommended" only; a modest incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed procedure for studies, encroachment lines and hearings; terms like "relative risk of flood" are technical but workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.2(a), Section 6.3 and Section 14.4(b)'s hearing rules, and expressly implemented by New York § 636.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Unwarranted constrictions" is a vague qualifier, but the acquisition power and its purposes are stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly tied to Section 6.2's standards and consistent with Section 14.14's condemnation power; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Lands particularly subject to flood" and "as conditions may warrant" are loose, but the power is merely to post and publish notices.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 6.2(b) and 3.6(d); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general promotional duty ("shall promote sound practices") with no measurable content, but nothing to apply against a party.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 7.2–7.4; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive grant to acquire, sponsor or operate soil-conservation projects; definite enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limited by Section 7.4(b)'s no-operation-if-others-available rule, which it expressly coexists with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear permissive grant relating to fish and wildlife habitats "related to the water resources of the basin."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 7.4 and 1.2(i); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A cooperation duty in general terms; "appropriate agencies" is soft but unremarkable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.9 and 11.5, and duplicated at Section 8.2(a); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "No other suitable unit or agency of government is available to operate the same upon reasonable conditions" turns on "suitable" and "reasonable conditions," both undefined and contestable. The finding requirement is otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restricts the operating powers granted in Sections 7.2, 7.3 and 3.6(a) and is anchored to Section 1.5, which it cites; that is a stated limitation rather than a conflict, though a party could argue Section 3.6(a) is broader.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Shall provide for the development of water related public sports and recreational facilities" mixes a mandatory duty with a permissive second sentence, leaving the strength of the obligation unclear. "Water related" is also loose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its mandate is qualified by Section 8.2(b), which forbids the commission from operating facilities others can operate; the two are harmonizable but in some tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard cooperation duty in general terms; nothing ambiguous of consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical in substance to Section 7.4(a) and consistent with Section 3.9; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same "suitable" and "reasonable conditions" vagueness as its Article 7 twin, applied to recreational facilities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies Section 8.1's development mandate and Section 8.3(c)'s operation duty, a limitation the compact states expressly and ties to Section 1.5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Within limits prescribed by this article" is a clear internal cross-limitation; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 8.1, 8.2 and 8.4; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An encouragement/coordination duty in wholly general terms; not an applied standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.9; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Recommend standards" is definite as to its non-binding character.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.6(b) and Section 6.2(a); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear duty to administer commission-owned facilities and let concessions "in accordance with this article."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers to Section 8.4's bidding rules and is limited by Section 8.2(b); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mandatory sealed-competitive-bid rule for concessions; "therefore" is a typo for "therefor" but nothing turns on it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15.1(l) expressly disapplies Section 8.4 to facilities operated under other federal law, an express carve-out rather than a conflict; Section 14.9's bid waivers do not by terms extend here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "May be impounded and used by or under authority of the commission ... in accordance with the comprehensive plan" is permissive and plan-bound; clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.2–9.4 and Section 13.1; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward permissive power to develop or authorize hydroelectric facilities.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.1 and 9.4; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Where such facilities are not otherwise available upon reasonable terms" is a soft condition, and the wholesale/direct-sale line could be argued at the margin. Those are namable but narrow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to Section 4.5's bar on water distribution and consistent with Section 2.7's power to sell power outside the basin; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Reasonable terms, consideration and duration" is a vague trio governing contract validity, though the notice-and-hearing requirement is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 9.2 and 14.4(b)'s hearing requirement; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Reasonable, nondiscriminatory, and just" is a triad of open-textured rate standards with no benchmark, exactly the kind of phrase parties contest. The terms are namable.
